To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

allergen exposure of sensitized guinea-pigs induces an upregulation of the contractile apparatus and a downregulation of the synthetic phenotype of the airway smooth muscle, resulting in an increased responsiveness to bronchospasmogenics.
the smooth muscle is a target for inflammatory mediators and that this leads to the development of bronchoconstriction and hyperreactivity.
smooth muscle cells of asthmatic airways are characterized by a proliferative-syndrom phenotype, which is associated with the expression of proinflammatory mediators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying the increased airway responsiveness in asthma.

the following aspects of airway smooth muscle function: (i) the role of smooth muscle cells in the development of bronchoconstriction and airway hyperreactivity, (ii) the mechanisms by which the airway smooth muscle cells are activated, (iii) the effects of inflammatory mediators and cytokines on smooth muscle cell function, (iv) the mechanisms by means of which smooth muscle cells contribute to airway inflammation, and (v) the mechanisms of airway smooth muscles remodeling.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of bronchial smooth muscle hyperreactivitiy, which is the main pathophysiologic feature of asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the airway smooth muscle cell is an active participant in the pathogenesis of bronchial asthma and that the smooth muscle is a potential target for therapeutic interventions.
smooth muscle cells play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of asthma and that they are a major target for the treatment of the disease.
the smooth muscle is not only the effector organ but also a key player in the pathogenesis of asthma and bronchial hyperreactivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in asthma the smooth muscle cell itself is not only the effector cell but also the target of the inflammatory response.
the airway smooth muscle cell is not only a contractile cell but also a highly reactive and inflammatory cell.
the smooth muscle cells are capable of producing inflammatory cytokines and chemotaxins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the smooth muscle cells of the bronchial tree are not just passive responders to the inflammatory environment but rather actively participate in the development of airway hyperresponsiveness and airway inflammation.
smooth muscle cells can be activated by a variety of stimuli, which leads to a change in their phenotype and function.

the smooth muscle is not a passive target of inflammatory cells and mediators but is a dynamic, active, and responsive cell type that is capable of contributing directly to the pathogenesis of airway disease in asthma.
